To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
5-Nitrofurfural-derived aminophosphonic acids are active against MRSA strains.
the antibacterial activity of aminophosphonic acids is not related to their imine precursors and that the presence of a nitro group at the furan ring is necessary for the activity.
aminophosphonic acids bearing 2-nitrifuran moiety were revealed to act against clinical isolates, especially against MRSA strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, and evaluation of the antibacterial activity of (5-nitrifurfuryl)-derivatized aminophosphonic acids and their parent imine derivatives.
the design and synthesis of novel antibacterial agents based on aminophosphonic acids and their parent imine compounds.
the design and synthesis of new compounds, which could be potential antibacterial agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aminophosphonic acid derivatives bearing 5-nitrofuran group are promising antibacterial agents.
the tested N-aryl 2-nitro-furralaldimines and their corresponding aminophosphonic acid derivatives have a moderate antibacterial activity, which was not accompanied by the cytotoxicity.

aminophosphonic acid derivatives with the 2-nitrofurane moiety in their structure, in general, possess a low antibacterial activity, while the imine precursors of these compounds are much more active and, at the same time, less toxic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antibacterial action of the studied compounds depends on their chemical structure and that the most active compounds are those with the O-methyl group and the 4-methoxy- and 4-methyl-substituted aryl group in the imine fragment.
aminophosphonic acids bearing a nitro group in 2-position of furan moiety are active against methicillin resistant strains of Staphylococcus aureus.
the antibacterial activity of the studied aminophosphonic acids depends on the structure of their 2-nitrofuranyl moieties, and the presence of the 2-nitrogen atom in this moiety is not necessary.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the imines of 5-nitrofuran-2-carbaldehyde are promising antibacterial agents, especially against MRSA strains, while their O,O′-substituted derivatives, especially O,O′-bis(4-methylphenethyl) aminophosphonic acid, are less active, but they do not show any toxicity.
aminophosphonic acids bearing 2-nutrofuran moiety are active against clinical isolates S. aureus and especially methicillin-resistant strains.

the O,O′-methyl and O,O-ethyl aminophosphates bearing 5-nitrofuran group are active against clinical isolates S. aureus (MRSA) and that N-aryl 2-nitro-5-furfuralaldimes are active in vitro and cytotoxic in vivo.
